title: Quietly Simmered Vietnamese Guanciale Nem Nuong
description: A cultured and comforting Vietnamese dish featuring guanciale, simmered to perfection in a flavorful broth, served in a bamboo tray, and vegan-friendly by substitution, in the form of nem nuong, perfect for a sick day, with a shattering crunch from the fried shallots and a rich, meaty flavor from the guanciale, which can be substituted with a vegan alternative to cater to different dietary needs.
instructions: In a large pot, combine the vegetable broth, lemongrass, and garlic, and bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Add the guanciale to the pot and simmer for 10 minutes, or until crispy and golden brown.
Remove the guanciale from the pot and set aside on a paper towel-lined plate to drain excess oil.
Add the rice vermicelli to the pot and cook for 3-5 minutes, or until tender.
In a small bowl, whisk together the fish sauce and 1 tablespoon of water, and set aside.
In a large skillet, heat 1 tablespoon of oil over medium heat, and add the sliced shallots, cooking until crispy and golden brown.

To assemble the nem nuong, place a portion of the cooked rice vermicelli on a bamboo tray, followed by a slice of the guanciale, a spoonful of the simmered broth, and a sprinkle of chopped scallions and peanuts.
Drizzle the fish sauce mixture over the top of the nem nuong and serve immediately, garnished with additional chopped scallions and peanuts if desired.
To make the dish vegan-friendly, substitute the guanciale with a vegan alternative, such as tofu or tempeh, and use a vegan fish sauce alternative.
Serve the nem nuong in the bamboo tray, garnished with crispy fried shallots and a sprinkle of chopped peanuts.
